A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same multimodal news-framing study. Their main text, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original MFC classifier evaluations, human annotation of images and topics, and corpus-level analyses of textual and visual framing.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical evaluations and corpus analyses, and adds annotation-agreement statistics, error diagnostics and issue-frame frequency results.

M1.justification: The Mistral-7B text and Pixtral-12B image annotation pipeline, generic multi-label framing and open-ended issue-frame generation remain unchanged. Listings 1–2 retain substantively identical prompts. The unsuccessful salience-ordering experiment is supplementary, not an adopted component.

E1.justification: The news corpus, MFC and main human-annotated evaluation sets are retained. v3 additionally reports exploratory prediction of frames in salience order in Section 8, introducing a limited ranking requirement beyond the unranked framing evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: Neither version reports an evaluated competing framing method or baseline model. Human annotations remain reference labels; additional citations and agreement statistics do not introduce comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 replaces image annotators' binary overlap measure with Krippendorff's alpha and mean Jaccard agreement. Appendix G specifies a new mismatch-counting procedure for error analysis. Main evaluation sample sizes and inference settings remain unchanged; Figure 10's revised caption does not establish a changed normalization procedure.

E4.justification: v1's brief classifier-performance appendix becomes substantial text and image error analysis in v3 Appendix G, including mismatch matrices, nine misclassification examples and analysis of zero-overlap image errors. Appendix H adds issue-frame diversity and topic-distribution analysis. v3 also reports a filtering-threshold audit and unsuccessful salience-ordering trials.

E5.justification: v3 replaces the reported 85% image-annotator overlap with Krippendorff's alpha of 0.393 and mean Jaccard index of 0.614, and newly reports 83.5% topic-annotation agreement. These change statistical reliability reporting, not demonstrated agreement under an identical metric. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Reported MFC overlap changes from 89.36% to 95.7%, and micro-F1 from 0.44 to 0.50. Table 4 changes legality precision/recall/F1 from 0/0/0 to 0.53/0.87/0.66, while other per-label scores remain unchanged. v3 also adds extensive mismatch counts and reports over 56,000 unique issue frames. The PDFs do not explain whether the revised MFC scores reflect correction or rerunning.

T1.justification: Appendix G introduces an explicit definition of the multi-label mismatch-frequency matrix: each missed gold label is paired with erroneous predictions, and these counts are summed across instances. This is a limited mathematical specification for the new diagnostic; no theorems, proofs or broader theoretical development are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal contributions retain the first computational multimodal news-framing study, scalable LLM/VLM annotation, the 500,000-article dataset, and framing differences across modalities and political leanings. Added research questions and the rewritten conclusion largely restate these contributions.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges equal weighting of predicted frames and the difficulty of estimating their salience. It adds possible causes of text-image differences, including image availability, search algorithms and editorial factors. Appendix G discusses plausible alternative frame interpretations and cautions that infrequent labels can explain low error counts.

D1.justification: v3 documents prompt variants more specifically, describes the image-sampling audit supporting the unchanged 5,000-byte filtering threshold, and clarifies that released image captions are not used in framing analysis. Model versions, decoding parameters, image resizing, hardware, runtime and dataset-access information remain substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: The shortened integrative-framing discussion removes Geise et al. (2013) and Matthes and Kohring (2008). v3 adds a frame-building interpretation using the already cited De Vreese (2005). Other reference edits largely supply bibliographic metadata, and the central novelty positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds explicit research questions, condenses and reorders the framing background, rewrites the conclusion, reorganizes appendix headings and removes acknowledgments. Much of the main analysis and the overall section sequence remain intact, so this is a localized revision rather than a wholesale rewrite.

P2.justification: v3 replaces Figure 1's illustrative example, redraws Figure 4 with a common vertical scale for text and image counts, and adds Tables 7–10 for diagnostics and issue-frame frequencies. It also relocates the extracted-aspects table and several existing figures. Figure 10 retains the same plotted content despite its revised caption.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's brief validation, v3's agreement statistics and Appendix G diagnostics make reliability and failure modes more assessable. Explicit salience limitations and Figure 4's common scale also improve interpretation. The gain is limited by unexplained MFC score revisions and unfinished wording in the new error-analysis appendix; higher reported scores alone do not establish improved quality.
